definitions.explanation: So painful, difficult, or unpleasant that it is extremely hard to bear or put up with.

examples.japanese: {耐|た}え{難|がた}い{痛|いた}みだ。
{耐|た}え{難|がた}い{暑|あつ}さの{中|なか}、{作業|さぎょう}を{続|つづ}けた。
examples.english: They continued working in the unbearable heat.

examples.japanese: {耐|た}え{難|がた}きを{耐|た}え、{忍|しの}び{難|がた}きを{忍|しの}び。
examples.english: Enduring the unendurable, bearing the unbearable.
examples.notes: Famous phrase from Emperor Showa's 1945 radio address announcing Japan's surrender.

notes:
Formed from {耐|た}える (to endure) + {難|がた}い (difficult to ~). A literary and formal expression for extreme difficulty in enduring something. Also written {耐|た}えがたい, with the がたい part in kana; both spellings are common.

CULTURAL CONTEXT:
The phrase {耐|た}え{難|がた}きを{耐|た}え、{忍|しの}び{難|がた}きを{忍|しの}び is one of the most famous lines in modern Japanese history, from the {玉音放送|ぎょくおんほうそう} (Imperial radio broadcast) on August 15, 1945, in which Emperor Showa announced Japan's surrender.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {耐|た}え{難|がた}い{痛|いた}み — unbearable pain
- {耐|た}え{難|がた}い{苦|くる}しみ — intolerable suffering
- {耐|た}え{難|がた}い{屈辱|くつじょく} — unbearable humiliation
- {耐|た}え{難|がた}い{暑|あつ}さ — unbearable heat

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {我慢|がまん}できない — can't stand it; more colloquial
- {信|しん}じ{難|がた}い — hard to believe; same ～{難|がた}い pattern
- {堪|た}えられない — unbearable; spoken/colloquial equivalent

forms.label: Conditional たら
forms.negative: {耐|た}え{難|がた}くなかったら
